paper_metadata.title: Mixed-Signal Quantum Circuit Design for Option Pricing Using Design Compiler

summary: The paper proposes a mixed-signal gate-based quantum circuit design for option pricing using Quantum Amplitude Estimation, introducing exponential data preprocessing and digital calibration. In a 12‑qubit statevector simulation, the optimized circuit reduces gate count from 4095 to 392 and circuit depth from 2048 to 6 relative to the JP Morgan option-pricing circuit, while reducing maximum calculation error from 25.86% to 1.64%. However, nonlinear payoff and exponential components are not yet implemented and results are demonstrated only in simulation.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit for option pricing using quantum amplitude estimation, with exponential data pre-processing and digital calibration compared against the JP Morgan option-pricing circuit.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) for option pricing with mixed-signal circuit optimizations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical preprocessing maps lognormal distribution / weighted averages into rotation angles; digital calibration uses lookup-table correction for rotation inputs. Option-pricing payoff is based on weighted averages and QAE measurement.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate option price / expected payoff via weighted average using QAE; paper references the JP Morgan option-pricing circuit and weighted-sum computation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Digital calibration via LUT-based angle correction; classical preprocessing isolates relevant payoff region before quantum circuit.

problem_instance.description: 12-qubit option-pricing case study based on the JP Morgan quantum option pricing circuit; includes lognormal distribution preprocessing and Monte Carlo-style price simulation components.
problem_instance.dataset_name: JP Morgan option pricing benchmark / lognormal distribution case study

dataset_specification.description: 12-qubit input; discretized into 32 output levels (0 to 31) with inputs ranging from 0 to 4095

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical preprocessing of piecewise linear payoff region; lognormal distribution discretization; LUT-based digital calibration of rotation angles; validation of linear portions only.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison against JP Morgan baseline; reported gate count, depth, and maximum calculation error before/after calibration.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preprocessing of payoff region and lognormal distribution; LUT-based angle correction.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison of circuit outputs to baseline error and Monte Carlo-style averages.

speedup_claims.conditions: 12-qubit case study; exponential data pre-processing optimization
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as gate-count reduction from 4095 to 392; not a runtime benchmark.

speedup_claims.conditions: 12-qubit case study; exponential data pre-processing optimization
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as depth reduction from 2048 to 6; not a runtime benchmark.
Computed from 25.86% to 1.64%; paper frames this as improved noise tolerance.

speedup_claims.factor: O(n^2) gate complexity and O(n) depth
speedup_claims.conditions: claimed for optimized exponential data pre-processing
speedup_claims.caveats: Stated as an expectation/claim rather than a measured asymptotic proof.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n^2) gate complexity and O(n) depth after optimization (claimed expectation for exponential data preprocessing)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large-scale fault-tolerant circuits implementing full option-pricing pipeline including nonlinear payoff and exponential functions with amplitude estimation.
limiting_factors: Only a 12-qubit statevector simulation is demonstrated.
Key nonlinear components (exponential and payoff functions) are explicitly not implemented.
Performance comparison is against another quantum circuit (JP Morgan) rather than classical runtime.
Gate-count and depth improvements do not translate to demonstrated computational speedup.
Heavy classical preprocessing (distribution discretization and LUT calibration) required before quantum execution.

notes: Hardware type is not explicitly named; Qiskit/statevector is mentioned for figures, so no real QPU is reported.
12 qubits, gate count 392, and depth 6 are explicitly reported in the experimental results.
The paper claims reduction from exponential to polynomial complexity (O(n^2) gates, O(n) depth) for preprocessing.
The paper claims circuit efficiency improvements and potential quantum advantage via QAE but does not experimentally demonstrate advantage over classical option pricing.
Results are limited to statevector simulations and circuit resource comparisons.
